A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Greed is Good, with complete, readable main text and appendices. Equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite the added checklist, implementation appendix, and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 7 and Appendix I report original FFHQ inverse-image experiments and QM9 molecular-generation results, including reconstruction, property-error, and molecular-stability measurements.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix J retain original FFHQ and QM9 results and add discretization-step experiments.

M1.justification: The greedy guidance procedure, DTO/OTD framework, models, and objectives remain unchanged. Additional step counts instantiate the existing numerical-solver framework, while Appendix G explains its implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight FFHQ inverse-image tasks and six QM9 molecular properties. The added step-budget experiments retain these datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 adds DTO as a comparator for HDR reconstruction in Table 2; v2's HDR comparison in Table 5 included DAPS, DPS, and RED-diff without DTO. RED-diff was therefore already present. The original QM9 DTO comparator is retained as DTO (50-step).

E3.justification: The added HDR ablation uses L-BFGS for greedy guidance, SGD for DTO, and a matched maximum of 100 optimization steps, unlike the retained image protocol's SGD with 50 optimization steps per ODE step. v3 also evaluates substantially more gradient-discretization budgets on HDR and QM9. These are additional protocols, not demonstrated revisions to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Tables 2–3 substantially expand analysis of the central discretization tradeoff through greedy and DTO step-count sweeps on HDR and QM9. v3 also reports instability with Ralston's third-order method. RK4 failures and attempted remedies were already documented in v2 Appendix H.2.

E5.justification: v2 already reports fixed seeds and uncertainty for several baselines. v3 newly specifies four runs per algorithm and reports means and standard deviations for the HDR ablation's greedy and DTO results. This does not establish increased run counts for retained experiments; no significance tests are added.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive HDR and QM9 step-budget results in Tables 2–3. It also revises all six QM9 two-step Euler MAEs, including polarizability from 5.377 to 5.667, without explaining the revision. The original image and molecular-stability tables are retained apart from equivalent rounding; the new HDR scores use separate experimental settings.

T1.justification: v3 adds Corollary D.1.2 on higher-order guidance dynamics and its short proof. Equation (79) corrects the Jacobian evaluation point from x + x_hat_j to x_hat_j, aligning it with Equation (76). The main theorems, assumptions, and remaining proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unifying posterior and end-to-end guidance through a greedy perspective, analyzing their gradients, and exploring the compute–accuracy tradeoff. Additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations favoring greedy guidance at small step budgets and describes full-step DTO as a performance upper bound. That bound is not universal in Table 3: one-step DTO has lower LUMO MAE than 50-step DTO, 86.512 versus 373. Existing limitations and broader-impact discussions are retained in Appendix K.

D1.justification: v3 adds implementation guidance in Appendix G, explicitly documents the 50-step Euler solver for QM9, and supplies optimizer and budget details for the HDR ablation. Its checklist also identifies seed configurations and planned supplementary code. Existing hardware, runtime, and most hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Daras et al.'s inverse-problem survey, He et al.'s manifold-preserving guidance, and Tong et al.'s conditional flow matching work. These modestly extend contextual discussion without changing the central research positioning. DAPS's publication update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized experimental discussion, a new implementation appendix and NeurIPS checklist, and wording, footer, and cross-reference updates. Most prose and the main narrative order remain intact; later appendices are renumbered rather than replaced.

P2.justification: v3 adds the HDR ablation table, expands and regroups the QM9 table, and adds entries to taxonomy Figure 5. Theorem callouts are restyled and some displays move. The qualitative image and molecule figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new step-budget sweeps provide more direct empirical support for the central guidance tradeoff, while implementation disclosures and the Equation (79) correction improve clarity. The gain is limited by different optimizers in the HDR comparison, unexplained QM9 score revisions, and the overly broad interpretation of full-step DTO as a performance upper bound.
